variants.stem: Find the exact value of each expression. Give each answer as an angle in radians.

parts.prompt: Find arcsin(√2/2).
Find arccos(1/2).
Find arctan(−1).

solution: sin(π/4) = √2/2, and π/4 is in [−π/2, π/2], so arcsin(√2/2) = π/4.

variants.stem: Each angle is found with an inverse trigonometric function. Round each answer to the nearest thousandth of a radian.

parts.prompt: A ramp rises 2.6 feet over a horizontal run of 7.5 feet. Find the angle the ramp makes with the ground.
A 20-foot ladder leans against a wall with its foot 2 feet from the wall. Find the angle the ladder makes with the ground.
A kite is 29 meters above the ground on a straight string that is 62 meters long. Find the angle the string makes with the ground.

solution: tan θ = rise/run = 2.6/7.5, so θ = arctan(2.6/7.5) ≈ 0.334 radians.
The foot of the ladder is adjacent to the angle and the ladder is the hypotenuse, so cos θ = 2/20 and θ = arccos(2/20) ≈ 1.471 radians.
The height is opposite the angle and the string is the hypotenuse, so sin θ = 29/62 and θ = arcsin(29/62) ≈ 0.487 radians.

variants.stem: Answer each question about the inverse trigonometric functions.

parts.prompt: To define y = arctan x, the tangent function is restricted to which interval of angles? Use interval notation.
State the domain of y = arccos x. Use interval notation.
State the range of y = arcsin x. Use interval notation.

solution: Tangent is restricted to (−π/2, π/2), where it is one-to-one and still takes every value in its range.
The input of arccos is a value of cos. Cosine takes values from −1 to 1, so the domain of arccos is [−1, 1].
The output of arcsin is an angle in the restricted domain of sin, so the range is [−π/2, π/2].

The output of arccos is an angle in the restricted domain of cos, so the range is [0, π].
The input of arctan is a value of tan. Tangent takes every real value, so the domain of arctan is (−∞, ∞).
